findings.where: How to set a variable > A `rinzler` service instance (lines 128-144). Rows CPUAFFINITY, RZ_CLI_ARGS, RZ_FUSE_MOUNT_PATH, SYSTEM_CONFIG, TRON_LOG_DIR.
findings.problem: The table says that a person writes `/opt/positron/user/config.env`, that the file applies to every instance, and that it wins over the instance file. Five rows marked Operators hold values that differ between instances. No sentence tells the reader to keep those values out of `config.env`. Likely wrong action: a support engineer wants to add one option and writes `RZ_CLI_ARGS=--kv-cache-gb 24` in `config.env`. systemd then replaces the platformd command line of every instance. The same mistake gives every instance one CPU list (`CPUAFFINITY`), one FUSE stats mount path (`RZ_FUSE_MOUNT_PATH`) and one log file (`TRON_LOG_DIR`).
findings.evidence: packaging/systemd/rinzler@.service:26 and :43 (file order), :53 (ExecStart expands both variables), :50 (the unit unmounts the path before each start). README.stats.md:45-47 (platformd writes RZ_FUSE_MOUNT_PATH per instance). src/system/spdlog.cpp:81 (the log file name has no instance id). systemd.exec(5), EnvironmentFile=: "the later setting will override the earlier setting".
findings.fix:
Add this bullet after the bullet that ends with "(systemd.exec(5), `EnvironmentFile=`).":

- `/opt/positron/user/config.env` holds one value for every instance, and it
  wins over the instance file. Do not put a value there that differs between
  instances: `CPUAFFINITY`, `RZ_CLI_ARGS`, `RZ_FUSE_MOUNT_PATH`, `TRON_LOG_DIR`,
  or a `SYSTEM_CONFIG` that holds `--instance`, `--devices`, `--app-cores`,
  `--dev-cores` or `--numa`. A value in this file replaces the platformd value.
  It does not add to it. Example: `RZ_CLI_ARGS=--kv-cache-gb 24` in this file

findings.fix:
Add these entries to "Words used here". Then remove the repeated inline definitions from the rows.

- **Forward pass**: one run of the model over a group of tokens. One request
  needs many forward passes.
- **Minibatch**: a group of tokens that one forward pass computes together.
- **Scheduler**: the part of `libtron` that chooses the tokens of each forward
  pass and requests KV cache memory for them.
- **Logits**: the scores that the model computes for every possible next
  token.
- **KV page**: 64 tokens of KV cache.
- **Arena allocator, legacy allocator**: the two allocators of the hugepage
  memory, with the code names `pos_heap_v2` and `pos_heap`. The arena
  allocator is the build default.
- **Resource map**: the YAML file that lists FPGA cards and CPU cores per
  server type.
- **Drop-in**: a systemd file that changes a unit without an edit of the unit
  file.
- **Chat template**: the template of a model that turns the messages of a
  request into the prompt text.
- **Speculative decoding**: a draft model proposes candidate tokens, and the
  main model then verifies them.
- **Rust tokenizer, Python tokenizer**: the Hugging Face library inside the
  process, and a helper program that runs as a child process.
- **Assertion**: a check in the code that stops the process with a message
  when it fails.
- **CMake option, preset**: settings of the build. Nobody can change them on
  an installed system.

Define the other terms in the cell that uses them, or replace them with plain words: "crate" with "Rust library", "made canonical" with "symbolic links are resolved", "scalar" with "a text, a number or a boolean".
